messages.subject: Trouble shooting with multi_normal_cholesky()
parts:
Hello,
I'm trying to tame stan and to use multi_normal_cholesky().
The following model compiles but then stan starts complaining and R crashes. Any idea of what I am doing wrong?
Here are the model and data

library(rstan)
library(mvtnorm)
my.dat <- list(n_obs = 50,
                    y = rmvnorm(50,c(-10,0,15),c(5,1,2)*diag(3))
                    )

my.code2 <- "
  data {
   int<lower=0> n_obs; 
   vector[3] y[n_obs];
  }
  parameters {
   vector[3] theta;
   real<lower=0> D[3];
  }
  transformed parameters {
   matrix[3,3] L;
   vector[3] lambda;
   matrix[3,3] chol_mat;
   lambda[1] <- D[1]; lambda[2] <- D[2]; lambda[3] <- D[3];
   L[1,1] <- 1; L[2,2] <- 1; L[3,3] <- 1;
   L[1,2] <- 0; L[1,3] <- 0; L[2,3] <- 0;
   chol_mat <- diag_matrix(lambda)*L;
  }
  model {
   L[2,1] ~ normal(0,0.5); L[3,1] ~ normal(0,0.5); L[3,2] ~ normal(0,0.5);
   for ( j in 1:3 ) {
    theta[j] ~ normal(0,100);
    D[j] ~ normal(0,1.5)T[0,];
   }
   for ( k in 1:n_obs ) {
    y[k] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(theta,chol_mat);
   }
  }
"

fit2 <- stan(model.code = my.code2, data = my.dat,
            n.iter = 10000, n.chains = 4)

I think the issue here is that the lower triangular elements of L are
never actually defined as parameters and are uninitialized. Try this:

my.code2 <- "
data {
int<lower=0> n_obs;
vector[3] y[n_obs];
}
parameters {
vector[3] theta;
real<lower=0> D[3];
vector[3] L_entries;

}
transformed parameters {
matrix[3,3] L;
vector[3] lambda;
matrix[3,3] chol_mat;
lambda[1] <- D[1]; lambda[2] <- D[2]; lambda[3] <- D[3];
L[1,1] <- 1; L[2,2] <- 1; L[3,3] <- 1;
L[1,2] <- 0; L[1,3] <- 0; L[2,3] <- 0;

L[2,1] <- L_entries[1]; L[3,1] <- L_entries[2]; L[3,2] <- L_entries[3];
chol_mat <- diag_matrix(lambda)*L;
}
model {
L_entries~ normal(0,0.5);

for ( j in 1:3 ) {
theta[j] ~ normal(0,100);
D[j] ~ normal(0,1.5)T[0,];
}
for ( k in 1:n_obs ) {
y[k] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(theta,chol_mat);
}
}
"

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Trouble shooting with multi_normal_cholesky()
parts:
On 9/2/12 11:19 AM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> I think the issue here is that the lower triangular elements of L are
> never actually defined as parameters and are uninitialized.

We shouldn't be crashing, whatever the user does!

This may be a case where we need to do more initialization
implicitly. I just added inits for all the transformed
parameters.

I think what we really need is a lower-triangularCholesky-factor-for-
covariance-matrix data type (i.e., lower triangular, positive diagonal)
and a name for it.

- Bob

> implicitly. I just added inits for all the transformed
> parameters.
>
> I think what we really need is a lower-triangularCholesky-factor-for-
> covariance-matrix data type (i.e., lower triangular, positive diagonal)
> and a name for it.
>
>
> I continue to think we need a covariance matrix class capable of representing a covariance matrix in a variety of ways
> that has a Cholesky factor attribute.

I agree. The Cholesky factor basic type is
just easier.

The issue with covariance matrices is caching,
so the following operation would be efficient:

matrix cholesky_factor(cov_matrix x);

(Right now, though, Stan doesn't include what kind of
matrix something is directly in the type checking. The
reason is that we don't guarantee that a cov_matrix
remains a cov_matrix. To do that, as we discussed before,
would require limiting the operations on it.)

Eventually, that could even use the Cholesky factor
basic type:

cov_matrix_cholesky_factor
cholesky_factor(cov_matrix x);

Then, I think the issue is how we cache the Cholesky
factor and recompute it if necessary in a lazy fashion.

- Bob
